title: Ordering food you can eat
title_target: កុម្ម៉ង់បាយ — kom-mang baay
goal: Order food and drinks correctly — including explaining what you don't eat in sentences that leave no room for misunderstanding.
bekal: order with សុំ … និង …
explain dietary restrictions with ខ្ញុំមិនញ៉ាំ …
ask for something without a certain ingredient using កុំដាក់ …
praise the food with ឆ្ងាញ់ណាស់
ask for the bill and pay

dialogs.title: កិច្ចសន្ទនា — A roadside noodle stall
dialogs.intro: Ani has her first lunch out. The most important sentence in this whole unit is in the fourth line — practice it until you can say it without thinking, if you need it, because you will say it almost every day in Cambodia.

lines.speaker: អ្នកបម្រើ:
lines.text: [បង|baang] [ញ៉ាំ|nyam] [អ្វី|'wey] [ចាស|chaah]?
lines.id: What would you like to eat?

lines.speaker: អានី:
lines.text: [មាន|mien] [អ្វី|'wey] [ខ្លះ|khlah] [ចាស|chaah]?

lines.speaker: អ្នកបម្រើ:
lines.text: [មាន|mien] [គុយទាវ|kuy-tiew], [បាយឆា|baay-chhaa], [អាម៉ុក|'aa-mok] [ចាស|chaah]។
lines.id: We have kuy teav, fried rice, amok.

lines.speaker: អានី:
lines.text: [ខ្ញុំ|khnyom] [មិន|min] [ញ៉ាំ|nyam] [សាច់ជ្រូក|sach-chruuk] [ទេ|té] [ចាស|chaah]។ [មាន|mien] [សាច់មាន់|sach-moan] [ទេ|té]?
lines.id: I don't eat pork. Do you have chicken?
lines.literal: I — not — eat — meat-pig — no — yes(f). have — meat-chicken — (question)?

lines.speaker: អ្នកបម្រើ:
lines.text: [មាន|mien] [ចាស|chaah]។ [គុយទាវ|kuy-tiew] [សាច់មាន់|sach-moan] [បាន|baan] [ទេ|té]?
lines.id: Yes. Is chicken kuy teav OK?

lines.speaker: អានី:
lines.text: [បាន|baan] [ចាស|chaah]។ [ប៉ុន្តែ|pon-tae] [កុំ|kom] [ដាក់|dak] [ទឹកត្រី|teuk-trey] [ច្រើន|chraeun] [ពេក|péék]។
lines.id: Yes. But not too much fish sauce.
lines.literal: can — yes(f). but — don't — put — water-fish — much — too.

lines.speaker: អ្នកបម្រើ:
lines.text: [បាទ|baat]។ [ហឹរ|hel] [បាន|baan] [ទេ|té]?

lines.speaker: អានី:
lines.text: [ហឹរ|hel] [បន្តិច|ban-tech] [បាន|baan] [ចាស|chaah]។ [កុំ|kom] [ហឹរ|hel] [ពេក|péék]។
lines.id: A little spicy is fine. Not too spicy.
lines.literal: spicy — a-little — can — yes(f). don't — spicy — too.

lines.speaker: អ្នកបម្រើ:
lines.id: What would you like to drink?

lines.speaker: អានី:
lines.text: [សុំ|som] [ទឹក|teuk] [មួយ|muèy] [ដប|daap] [ចាស|chaah]។ [កុំ|kom] [ដាក់|dak] [ទឹកកក|teuk-kaak]។
lines.id: A bottle of water, please. No ice.
lines.literal: ask-for — water — one — bottle — yes(f). don't — put — water-frozen.

lines.speaker: អ្នកបម្រើ:
lines.text: [បាទ|baat]។ [សូម|soum] [រង់ចាំ|roang-cham] [បន្តិច|ban-tech]។

lines.speaker: អានី:
lines.text: [ឆ្ងាញ់|chhngañ] [ណាស់|nah] [ចាស|chaah]! [សុំ|som] [គិតលុយ|ket-luy] [ផង|phaang]។
lines.literal: delicious — very — yes(f)! ask-for — count-money — too.

grammars.title: ⚠️ Explaining what you don't eat so it really gets understood
body: This is one of the most important sections of the course if you have dietary restrictions — religious, vegetarian, or medical — and it is deliberately placed early. Khmer has no word for "halal" or "kosher" that every food stall understands, so the safest approach is **to name what you don't eat, not to ask for a category**.

head: English
Khmer
Say it
rows: ខ្ញុំមិនញ៉ាំសាច់ជ្រូកទេ
ខ្ញុំជាមូស្លីម
មានសាច់មាន់ទេ?
នេះមានសាច់ជ្រូកទេ?
ខ្ញុំមិនផឹកស្រាទេ
ខ្ញុំញ៉ាំបួស

after: ⚠️ **Ask about pork specifically; don't ask "is there meat in it?"** In Cambodia, សាច់ (*sach*, meat) with nothing added almost always means pork — just as it often does in Chinese eateries. Asking "is there meat?" gets the answer "yes" and settles nothing.

⚠️ **Pork stock and fish sauce are almost everywhere.** The broth of គុយទាវ is usually made with pork bones. If this matters to you, look for halal restaurants — in Phnom Penh they cluster around the Nurul Ihsan mosque, Chraing Chamres, and Boeung Kak; in Siem Reap around Wat Damnak. The word **ហាឡាល់** (*haa-lal*) is understood in those restaurants, but not necessarily at roadside stalls.
**ញ៉ាំបួស** (*nyam buèh*, "eat vegetarian") is a phrase every Cambodian knows, because it is tied to Buddhist fasting days. If things get difficult, this is the fallback sentence that always works.

grammars.title: សុំ, កុំ, and ពេក — three short words for ordering
body: Almost every order you make can be built from these words. They never change form.

head: Word
Say it
Meaning
Example
rows: សុំទឹកមួយដប — a bottle of water, please
សូមរង់ចាំ — please wait
កុំដាក់ទឹកកក — no ice
ហឹរពេក — too spicy
សុំគិតលុយផង — the bill, please

after: ⚠️ Note that **ពេក stands after** the adjective — the reverse of English "too", which comes before. ហឹរពេក ("spicy too"), not ពេកហឹរ. It's the same logic as adjectives coming after nouns: in Khmer, the describing word follows.

grammars.title: Praising, complaining, and paying
body: Praising the food in Cambodia isn't just politeness — it's part of eating together, and saying nothing at all reads as not liking it.

head: English
Khmer
Say it
rows: ឆ្ងាញ់ណាស់!
មិនទាន់ឆ្អិន
ខ្ចប់បានទេ?

after: គិតលុយ (*ket-luy*) literally means "count the money", and it's how you ask for the bill all over Cambodia — at roadside stalls and air-conditioned restaurants alike. Raising your hand and miming writing in the air, the European habit, isn't understood here.

blocks.title: Three things about the Cambodian table
items: **Rice is the word for eating.** បាយ (*baay*) means rice, but ញ៉ាំបាយ ("eat rice") means eating anything. The question ញ៉ាំបាយហើយឬនៅ? ("Have you eaten rice yet?") is an everyday greeting, the equivalent of "how are you?".
**All the dishes arrive together and are shared.** Ordering "one just for me" feels odd; the natural thing is to order several plates for the whole table.
**Ice in the cities is generally made from clean water**, but if your stomach isn't used to it yet, កុំដាក់ទឹកកក (no ice) is a sentence that never offends anyone.
